title: Forensics Evidenceflow & SIEM Adapter Guidance
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures pragmatic implementation guidance for an evidence-oriented SIEM adapter and the attendant "forensics" evidenceflow that Security & Compliance (S&C) will adopt for RBAC v2 + audit log collection. Focus: how collectors should transform, enrich, and deliver control evidence so downstream auditors, SIEM rules, and automated evidence-harvest pipelines can operate deterministically.

Audience:
- S&C engineers implementing or reviewing collectors and adapters
- Infra/Platform engineers building transport/ingest components
- Solutions engineers responsible for evidence collection SLAs

Scope:
- Canonical audit-event shaping and minimal field set required for control evidence (RBAC changes, policy evaluations, admin actions)
- SIEM adapter options (syslog, HTTP JSON, Kafka) and schema examples
- Collector responsibilities (local buffering, retry, encryption, PII redaction)
- Evidenceflow runbook for control evidence capture and verification
- QA checklist and rollout guardrails

High-level architecture notes:
- Collectors sit at three logical points: control-plane services (authz, role mgmt), control-plane proxies (API gateway), and host-level agents (audit hooks).
- Each collector emits a normalized audit record to a local buffer, tags it with evidence metadata, and forwards to a primary transport (Kafka topic or HTTPS ingest endpoint).
- A dedicated SIEM Adapter service subscribes to the transport, applies enrichment (user directory lookup, model variant mapping, policy id mapping), and forwards to SIEM and the Evidence Ingest pipeline.

Minimal canonical audit-event (single-line JSON sample):
{
  "ts":"2025-11-28T14:22:03Z",
  "evt_id":"evt_8f3a2b",
  "service":"rbac-service",
  "actor":{"id":"user:amaiden@redwood.com","type":"user","ctx":{"ip":"198.51.100.12"}},
  "action":"role.binding.update",
  "targets":[{"type":"role","id":"role:duty-admin"}],
  "outcome":"success",
  "request_id":"req_0b4c",
  "evidence_context":{"policy_id":"POL-378","decision_trace":"trace://decisions/1234"},
  "schema_version":"cc-1.0",
  "sensitive_fields_masked":false
}

Key field definitions (required):
- ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamp (producer time)
- evt_id: globally-unique event id (uuid4 or event-prefixed id)
- service: logical service name emitting event
- actor: who initiated action (user, service, token). Must include canonical identity (email or service principal).
- action: dot-delimited verb (e.g., role.binding.create, policy.eval, token.rotate)
- targets: list of objects describing affected resources (type + id)
- outcome: success | failure | unknown
- evidence_context: free-form map for audit traceability (policy id, decision id, customer id). Must contain at least one linking identifier for control evidence retrieval.
- schema_version: version of our canonical audit schema
- sensitive_fields_masked: boolean flag - collector must set true if any PII was removed

SIEM Adapter transport patterns and guidance:
1) Kafka-first (recommended for internal regions):
   - Collectors publish to topic 'audit.events.cc' partitioned by service.
   - Payload: canonical JSON as above. Compression: snappy.
   - Adapter subscribes, performs idempotent processing (use evt_id as dedupe key), enriches, and emits to SIEM sink.
   - Advantages: high-throughput, backpressure support, easier replay for auditors.

2) HTTPS JSON (for cross-region / partner export):
   - Collector POST /ingest/audit with batch of records.
   - TLS mutual auth for private deployments.
   - Adapter must accept batches, return 207 Multi-Status for partial failures.
   - Rate-limit and backoff guidance documented in collector SDK.

3) Syslog (legacy / 3rd party SIEM connectors):
   - Emit normalized JSON payload as single-line syslog content.
   - Include schema_version and evt_id in log text.
   - Use forwards-to-syslog when adapter not available.

Collector responsibilities checklist:
- Accept structured events from app code (no free-text blobs for control evidence).
- Enforce field-level schema validation before buffering.
- Local on-disk circular buffer for up to 72 hours of events when network is offline.
- Exponential retry with jitter; non-destructive retries (preserve evt_id).
- Encrypt at rest using node-managed KMS keys; use TLS for transport.
- Mask PII according to S&C redaction rules; set sensitive_fields_masked=true when masking occurs and include redaction_reason in evidence_context.
- Attach minimal environment metadata: region, cluster id, node id, binary version.

RBAC considerations for evidence collection:
- Collector endpoints must accept only authenticated requests (service tokens or mTLS).
- Service tokens used by collectors should be scoped narrowly (collector:publish only).
- RBAC v2 events must include 'policy_id' and 'decision_trace' in evidence_context so policy rollbacks and audits can replay decision path.
- For role changes, collectors must emit both before_state and after_state diffs when possible; if not feasible, include a pointer to the authoritative snapshot (e.g., s3://snapshots/roles/2025-11-28T14:20Z.json).

Control evidence capture workflow (operational steps):
- Step 0: Precondition checks - collector installed, schema version verified, clock sync (NTP), credentials present.
- Step 1: Event generation - service emits canonical event synchronously as part of control operation.
- Step 2: Local persistence - collector validates and writes to write-ahead buffer atomically.
- Step 3: Forwarding - collector streams to primary transport with immediate ack semantics (on success mark buffer entry completed).
- Step 4: Adapter enrichment - Adapter enriches with dir-lookup and policy metadata; attaches audit_bucket pointer for raw evidence.
- Step 5: Evidence-indexing - Ingest pipeline indexes event into Evidence DB and routes copy to SIEM with retention tags.
- Step 6: Verification - Periodic audit job replays sample events, fetches linked artifacts (snapshots, diffs), and validates hash/signature.

Runbook / Troubleshooting quick checklist:
- If no events appear in SIEM for a service: check collector logs -> buffer backlog -> adapter subscription -> consumption lag metrics (Kafka consumer lag).
- If mask flag true but raw fields appear downstream: verify collector redaction config and KMS access.
- For duplicate events: verify dedupe key (evt_id) uniqueness and adapter idempotency.
- For partial batch failures over HTTPS: examine 207 responses and retry failed event ids only.

Data retention, privacy and compliance notes:
- Evidence DB stores canonical events for 1 year by default; SIEM retention depends on contract but adapter tags retention_policy on forwarded events.
- PII in control evidence is discouraged. If required for investigation, collectors must encrypt PII at field level and log who accessed it.
- For private deployments, customers may set stricter retention and masking policies; adapters must honor policy headers passed from ingest.

QA and testing plan (minimal):
- Unit tests for collector schema validation (+/- malformed fields).
- Integration test: simulate 1k control events/min into local Kafka and validate adapter enrichment and SIEM sink records.
- Replay test: store a day of events, run replay through adapter and ensure idempotent ingestion (no duplicates) and event hash stability.
- Red-team test: attempt to inject malformed actor identities, validate rejection and alerting.

Rollout guardrails:
- Start with a canary namespace (one microservice) for 2 weeks with elevated observability (event-level tracing enabled).
- Maintain feature flag for full forwarding; default to buffered-only for 72 hours after install.
- Gate production rollout on: zero critical schema violations, consumer lag < 10s, successful replay validation.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should the adapter perform on-the-fly PII tokenization or should that be collector-side only? (security prefers collector-side).
- Final naming convention for evt_id (uuid4 vs prefixed monotonic id).
- Evidence snapshot retention default for customers in private deployments.

Actions:
- P1: Add 'policy_id' enforcement to collector SDK validators (owner: Priya) - due 2025-12-05.
- P2: Implement 207 handling in SDK (owner: Liam) - due 2025-12-12.
- P3: Draft customer-facing guidance for private deployment retention settings (owner: Mateo) - due 2025-12-10.

Notes (informal):
- This doc intentionally uses the term 'forensics' to emphasize deterministic replayability over noisy telemetry.
- We should avoid adding free-text 'notes' fields in canonical events; use evidence_context pointers instead.

Appendix A - Example Kafka consume-enrich-forward flow (high-level):
- consumer reads batch -> validate evt_ids -> lookup actor metadata (cache TTL 5m) -> attach policy mapping -> write to SIEM sink and Evidence DB in single transactional flow (if sink supports at-least-once, mark processed in offset manager after ack).

Appendix B - Example redaction header (collector-to-adapter)::
- X-Evidence-Redaction: {"masked_fields":["actor.email"],"redaction_policy":"SENSITIVE_MASK_V2"}

If you are implementing a collector or reviewing a PR, use this doc as the source of decisions and file any deviations as a design note and link them to JIRA-SEC-492.
